differences.title: 1. STORAGE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: JetStream models durability around named Streams that contain messages with sequence numbers. Storage is per stream; leaders replicate state, and consumers fetch from the stream’s history via consumer offsets and ack state.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka models durability as append-only records in per-topic partitions. Producers write to a partition log; brokers maintain segment files and indexes, enabling fast sequential reads, retention policies, and replays from offsets.

differences.title: 2. CONSUMER SEMANTICS
differences.leftDesc: JetStream consumers are first-class objects with explicit acknowledgement behavior. Delivery supports push or pull; the server tracks per-consumer state (ack floor, redelivery, and replay windows) to guarantee at-least-once.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka consumer groups coordinate partition ownership. Each consumer tracks offsets in a group; commits (auto or manual) determine where the group resumes. Rebalance transfers partitions, and delivery is at-least-once with careful offset commits.

differences.title: 3. REPLICATION & LEADERING
differences.leftDesc: JetStream uses Raft-based replication for stream metadata and log consistency across replicas. A stream leader commits entries when a quorum of replicas acknowledges, then followers catch up for linearizable sequence progression.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka uses a leader/follower model with an in-sync replicas (ISR) set. The broker writes to the leader, and durability depends on producer acks and ISR quorum; lagging followers may be excluded from ISR.

differences.title: 4. RETENTION & REPLAY
differences.leftDesc: JetStream retention is configured at the stream level (by limits like max age, size, and number). Consumers can replay from a selected start position, bounded by what the stream has not yet trimmed.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka retention is configured at the topic (and ultimately partition) level using time-based and size-based log limits. Consumers replay from offsets as long as segments still exist; trimming can make old offsets invalid.

differences.title: 5. BACKPRESSURE & FLOW CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: JetStream push delivery is governed by per-consumer flow control using acknowledgements and server-side in-flight limits. Pull consumers fetch batches with explicit limits, reducing overload by shaping request rates.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka brokers and clients coordinate backpressure via fetch requests and server-side limits like max bytes per partition and request size. Consumer fetch loops and pause/resume behaviors handle lag and throughput constraints.

differences.title: 6. MESSAGE HEADER & SCHEMA ENVELOPES
differences.leftDesc: JetStream messages ride on NATS protocol envelopes, carrying subject-based routing plus JetStream metadata. Kafka emphasizes integration with schema tooling (e.g., Schema Registry) for evolution, while headers remain optional metadata.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka transports key/value plus optional headers inside the record batch. The ecosystem commonly pairs Kafka with Schema Registry for compatibility checks, and consumers decode formats independently from broker storage.

differences.title: 7. OPERATIONAL SURFACE AREA
differences.leftDesc: JetStream is built into the NATS server, so operators manage fewer moving parts: subjects, streams, and consumers. Scaling concentrates on stream placement and replica counts rather than many partition-level objects.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka requires managing a broker cluster and partitioning strategy across topics. Operational concerns include replication factor, leader election, rebalancing, log segment tuning, and monitoring across many partitions and consumers.
